name: New entrants and other land-finance providers (scan)
summary: 2025-2026 brought new, large balance sheets into builder land finance. Apollo launched Olympus Housing Capital (June 2025; about $1B executed land banking per trade press; CEO Andrew Brausa, a Domain co-founder per Apollo's release). Blackstone's real estate debt arm announced a homebuilder lending platform (May 2026; product mix unclear). Blue Owl is funding FivePoint's Hearthstone (up to $1.7B), Guggenheim/Bedrock, Starwood/Trez, and Wafra/Hunt's Strata Land Partners (Nov 2026) all launched land vehicles, and Walton Global, Avila and builder-affiliated lenders (Rooftop Capital, All Pro Capital) publish lot-finance programs. Older names (Värde, Brookfield) were quiet. KKR, Ares and Oaktree showed no public builder land finance. Most of these name no builders and publish no terms, so this is a map of who has capital, not of who has won share.

facts.fact: IHP Capital Partners: agreed to acquire 1,458 acres in Brazoria County, Texas (south Houston) for the Peachtree master plan, closing in phases; the first phase closed with 206 acres and 535 finished single-family lots. IHP posted the acquisition on its news page on 2026-09-30; reported by IREI on 2026-11-03 in an interview with co-president Richard Whiteley, who said the firm uses uncertain periods to secure land in high-growth markets. (Only the article's free opening was readable.)
facts.source_title: IREI: IHP Capital Partners sees long-term housing opportunities amid near-term market uncertainty

facts.fact: Forestar Group: at 2026-09-30 it owned about 58,200 lots and controlled about 26,200 more through purchase contracts (84,400 total). About 21,500 owned lots (37%) were under contract to sell, worth about $2.2 billion of future revenue; 19,800 of those were under contract to D.R. Horton and a further 18,600 owned lots (32%) were subject to D.R. Horton's right of first offer.
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-09-30) revenue was $1,635.1 million on 13,545 lots sold (5,004 lots and $580.8 million in Q4); pre-tax income $192.1 million, net income $142.6 million ($2.78 per diluted share). Lots sold to customers other than D.R. Horton were 1,916 in the year (822 in Q4), i.e. about 14% of lots sold (calculated: 1,916 / 13,545).
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: of 13,545 lots sold in fiscal 2026 (down 5% from 14,240), 1,916 went to customers other than D.R. Horton (2,489 in fiscal 2025); that 1,916 includes 146 lots sold for $33.4 million to a lot banker that expects to resell them to Horton (927 such lots in fiscal 2025). Horton therefore took about 11,629 lots directly, 86% (calculated: 13,545 less 1,916). Only 116 lots came from Forestar's own short-term 'lot banking projects' (348 in fiscal 2025).
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, MD&A

facts.fact: Forestar Group: fiscal 2026 investment was $270.1 million to acquire residential land and about $1.0 billion to develop it. Only about 8,100 of its 58,200 owned lots were fully developed at 2026-09-30 (8,900 a year earlier).
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, MD&A

facts.fact: Apollo: Commercial Observer's 2026 Power Investors profile of Apollo real estate equity head Bert Crouch (published 2026-07-30) says Apollo has executed about $1 billion of land banking through Olympus Housing Capital, roughly 13 months after launch. The same profile notes Apollo's private equity business owns top-25 builder Risewell Homes and that Apollo is in advanced talks to add a build-to-rent vertical. No builders, lot counts or yields are given.
facts.source_title: Commercial Observer, Power Investors 2026: Bert Crouch (2026-07-30)

facts.fact: Walton Global: sold 35 acres (198 lots) in Phase 2 of its Lake Ridge Parkway master plan in Ellis County, Texas (Dallas-Fort Worth) to Meritage Homes; price not disclosed. Reported 2026-07-16.
facts.source_title: AltsWire: Walton Global sells 35 acres to Meritage Homes at Lake Ridge Parkway

facts.fact: IHP Capital Partners: joint venture with Indianapolis builder Onyx+East for Trillium, an $80 million, 119-home community on 44 acres in Westfield, Indiana (base prices about $630,000 to $856,000; land about $116,000 to $120,000 per acre ready to build). Site closing and JV were announced May 2026. The article says IHP has completed 44 housing projects in Orange County and has also invested in Indianapolis, Cincinnati and Columbus.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: IHP Expands Beyond Orange County with $80M Indiana Project

facts.fact: Walton Global: its own release (2026-06-12) confirms eight Finished Lot Program closings in April and May 2026 totalling 525 lots: Houston 247 lots (Baron Village 183, Magnolia Meadows at Holly Ridge 40, Williams Reserve East 24), Dallas-Fort Worth 103 (Wildcat Ranch 50, Bluestem 53), Wellen Park, Florida 123 (Palmera 47, Edgewater 76) and Riverlake in the Wilmington, NC area 52. Deal sizes are 24 to 183 lots; no builder is named.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: strengthens land portfolio with acquisitions across key southern growth regions

facts.fact: Pretium: by 2026-05-07 Pretium said it had passed $3 billion of residential lending since its December 2024 platform launch, supporting more than 13,000 housing units, across single-family for-sale and rental construction and multifamily. It targets mid-sized builders producing 200 to 2,000 homes a year and originates with its affiliate Anchor Loans. The coverage describes construction-type lending and does not mention land banking or lot options.
facts.source_title: Pulse 2.0: Pretium Surpasses $3 Billion In Financing To Homebuilders And Multifamily Developers (2026-05-07)

facts.fact: Walton Global: in February and March 2026 its Builder Land Finance platform closed eight properties totalling about 1,392 lots in Texas, Florida, Georgia and Arizona, seven of them through its Finished Lot Program. The six communities listed are Cascada in the Tucson area (638 lots, 105 acres), three Dallas-Fort Worth properties (366 lots combined) Bridle Creek in Jacksonville (230 lots), Indian Springs in Houston (80), South Wind in Atlanta (54) and Oakfield Trails in western Florida (24). No builder was named.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: acquires eight properties in key Sunbelt markets

facts.fact: Walton Global: the 64-lot Sarasota purchase (expanding Oakfield Lakes, Finished Lot Program, release dated 2026-02-23) is one of four 2026 lot announcements. Calculated from Walton's own releases: 130 (Gemini, January) + 64 (Sarasota, February) + about 1,392 (February-March batch) + 525 (April-May batch) = about 2,111 lots acquired January to May 2026. The Sarasota lots may overlap with the February-March batch, so treat about 2,100 as an upper estimate.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: acquisition of 64 residential lots in Sarasota

facts.fact: Walton Global: 130 residential lots acquired at the Gemini community in Splendora, Texas through the Finished Lot Program, announced 2026-01-27; no builder, price or takedown schedule disclosed.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: expands Texas presence with newest acquisition near Houston

facts.fact: Walton Global: sold about 245 acres of its Lee Farm (Pinecrest) master plan in Loveland, Colorado to Forestar Group (release dated 2025-08-07); the plan is about 1,016 homes at build-out and Forestar is to deliver finished lots to D.R. Horton. Price not disclosed. Shows Walton acting as land seller to Horton's lot developer as well as financier.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: sells 245 acres to Forestar in Loveland, Colorado

facts.fact: Värde Partners: the last land-banking announcement found on Värde's own site is the 2024-04-04 joint venture with David Weekley Homes (Värde provides the land banking facility, David Weekley sources and develops), which had closed two Phoenix projects with over $100 million of project costs and targeted Phoenix, Tampa, Atlanta, Orlando and Charlotte. Facility size was not disclosed. This is older than 24 months with no newer public confirmation, hence Inferred as to current status.
facts.source_title: Värde press release: Värde Partners and David Weekley Homes Announce Land Banking Joint Venture (2024-04-04)

facts.fact: Brookfield: the only sized public reference found to Brookfield's lot-banking ambitions is a PERE teaser dated 2021-06-09 saying that, through its Newland acquisition, Brookfield had control of over 80,000 lots and wanted to bring scale to residential lot banking (article body paywalled). Older than 24 months with no newer confirmation, hence Inferred.
facts.source_title: PERE: Why Brookfield wants to bring scale to residential lot banking (2021-06-09, teaser only)

facts.fact: Land banking market: consultant Scott Cox (SLC Advisors) wrote on 2026-11-18 that 2027 will be a land negotiation year: builders may refuse to pay a land banker a 10% carry and may instead offer sellers rolling takedowns with a 3% annual escalator; he expects 'meaningful re-trades, not just extensions', especially for newer land bankers, and expects land prices (not only terms) to correct. Opinion piece, not disclosed deal terms.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Why 2027 may turn into a land negotiation year for homebuilders

facts.fact: Builder lending market: NAHB's Q3 2026 AD&C survey, as reported 2026-11-13, put effective borrowing costs (contract rate plus points, annualised) at 10.55% for land acquisition, 11.69% for land development, 11.83% for speculative single-family construction and 11.47% for pre-sold construction; contract rates were 8.08%, 7.83%, 7.72% and 7.27%. Credit tightened for a 19th straight quarter (NAHB net easing index -15.3; Fed -15.5).
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Builder credit conditions tighten for 19th straight quarter

facts.fact: Market context for entrants (not firm-specific): The Builder's Daily (2026-10-16) reports that Essential Housing's land-bank arrangements typically cost builders 200 to 250 basis points above their blended cost of capital, and that Essential Housing has originated over $22 billion of land-bank investments in five years and is raising capital for about $10 billion more.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Housing M&A shifts as global capital retargets residential futures (2026-10-16)

facts.fact: Builder lending market: NAHB survey averages for Q2 2026, as cited by The Builder's Daily on 2026-09-01, were about 10.43% for land acquisition loans, 12.59% for land development loans and 11.82% for speculative single-family construction loans (effective rates). Useful as the bank / private-credit alternative a builder compares a land-bank option fee against.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: AREC $305M California land facility

facts.fact: Land banking market: Launch DFA's sponsored article of 2026-05-20 cites roughly 12% as the industry cost of funding through private land-bank funds, contrasted with Millrose's lower cost of capital.
facts.source_title: HousingWire sponsored content (Launch DFA): infrastructure finance and land banking

facts.fact: Market context for entrants (not firm-specific): a June 2025 HousingWire column by Scott Cox of SLC Advisors says new land-bank funds typically charge builders about 11%, run roughly 45% leverage at about SOFR plus 200 basis points and so reach mid-teens returns on equity, and calls Millrose's 8.5% pooled rate to Lennar (about 7% after management fees) exceptionally low and a level that could push other participants out.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Understanding homebuilding's new capital partner, land banking, by Scott Cox (2025-06-04)

facts.fact: Walton Global: its Builder Land Financing page describes the structure only in outline: Walton buys land identified by a homebuilder client, charges the builder a premium, pays investors current interest semi-annually or quarterly and returns principal pro rata as homes are built and sold ('just-in-time' inventory). No fee rate, deposit or takedown terms are published.
facts.source_title: Walton Global: Builder Land Financing page

facts.fact: Forestar Group: D.R. Horton owned about 62% of Forestar at 2026-09-30. Under the Master Supply Agreement Horton has a right of first offer on up to 100% of lots in Horton-sourced projects and up to 50% of lots in the first phase of Forestar-sourced projects (and 50% of later phases if it bought at least 25% of the prior phase); no right on third-party-sourced deals. The agreement runs to the earlier of Horton holding under 15% of the vote or 2037-06-29. Forestar operated in 65 markets in 24 states with 408 employees and sold fiscal 2026 lots at an average price of $111,200.
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, Item 1

facts.fact: Värde Partners: Värde's real estate strategy page (retrieved 2026-11-19) still lists land banking partnerships that finance the creation of residential lots for sale to homebuilders as a current capital-solutions theme. It gives only firm-wide real estate figures ($24 billion-plus invested, 415-plus investments, 15 investment professionals) and no named platform, dollar size, lot count or builder list for land banking.
facts.source_title: Värde Partners website: Real Estate strategy page (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Brookfield: Brookfield Residential's land website (retrieved 2026-11-19, footer copyright 2024) markets a 'Land Banking' offering that gives homebuilders structured, stable capital for balance-sheet flexibility, but discloses no deal terms, capital amount, builders or lot counts (its 'Managed Lots' and 'Active Land Banks' counters display zero, apparently unpopulated).
facts.source_title: Brookfield Residential Land website (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital's own website (retrieved 2026-11-19) describes itself as an Apollo affiliate with access to long-duration capital, offering financing for residential land acquisition and development (planning and engineering through utilities, roads and amenities), customized investment structures and an 'off-balance sheet homesite supply' for homebuilders, with post-closing asset management. That is land-banking language, though the site never uses the words 'land banking' and lists no capital deployed, lots, offices or builder customers.
facts.source_title: Olympus Housing Capital website (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Hearthstone: its website still describes three lines: land banking and model sale-leaseback for public builders, joint-venture financing for private builders (up to 97% of the capital) and advisory; it claims over $18.0 billion committed to for-sale homebuilding across more than 700 communities. The site's newest news item is from 2024 and it does not mention FivePoint or Blue Owl, so it is stale against the 2025-2026 filings.
facts.source_title: Hearthstone website home page

facts.fact: Builders Capital: describes itself as a residential construction lender (tradename of Construction Loan Services II, LLC, part of the Builders Capital Exchange / BCX network; Puyallup, Washington). Products are an all-in-one acquisition, development and construction facility, new-construction lines, build-to-rent and bridge loans; it claims $17 billion+ of projects financed, 500+ builders, 18,000+ homes, 15,000+ lots developed and exposure of up to $350 million per builder. It does not offer lot-option land banking.
facts.source_title: Builders Capital website home page

facts.fact: Starwood: on 2026-11-03 Starwood Capital Group and Trez Capital announced a partnership to originate residential land acquisition-and-development (A&D) loans for single-family communities across the US, seeded with a $450 million portfolio of US residential land A&D loans originated by Trez and targeting more than $1 billion of originations a year. It is horizontal development lending, not lot-option land banking; loan sizes, pricing and borrowers were not disclosed.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Starwood / Trez Capital residential land lending (2026-11-06)

facts.fact: IHP Capital Partners: its 2025-2026 news flow is equity joint ventures with private builders and master-plan development, not lot-option land banking. Items on its news page: townhome JVs with The Grupe Company (San Ramon, 2.5 acres, posted 2025-09-18; Pleasanton, 2.6 acres, posted 2026-11-04) and Intracorp Homes (Alhambra, 2 acres, 2025-04-28); a first for-sale community with Onyx+East in Westfield, Indiana (2026-05-15); and the 1,458-acre Peachtree acquisition in Brazoria County, Texas (posted 2026-09-30).
facts.source_title: IHP Capital Partners: news page

facts.fact: Wafra / Hunt Companies (name surfaced by search): Strata Land Partners launched in early November 2026, backed by Wafra (about $30 billion AUM) and Hunt Companies, to provide land financing and lot-development capital to public and private builders nationwide, with a mandate described as broader than traditional land banking. It starts with projects totalling about 1,300 single-family lots and is led by Michael Forsum, former Landsea Homes president and COO and a Starwood Land Ventures alumnus. Capital commitment and builder customers were not disclosed.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Strata Land Partners launch (2026-11-02)

facts.fact: Strata Land Partners: a new land-finance platform launched 2026-11-02, backed by Wafra (about $30 billion AUM) and Hunt Companies and led by Michael Forsum, former president and COO of Landsea Homes. It offers land financing and lot-development capital to public and private builders, with a stated tilt to private builders; its first projects total about 1,300 single-family lots. Committed capital was not disclosed.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Strata Land Partners launch

facts.fact: Forestar Group: fiscal 2027 guidance is 12,000 to 13,000 lots delivered and $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion of revenue, i.e. flat to down against fiscal 2026's 13,545 lots and $1.64 billion.
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: GTIS Partners: renamed itself Brightshore Capital (reported 2026-09-15) after buying out minority partner GoldenTree Asset Management in 2025; about $5.6 billion of assets. It launched its first dedicated debt vehicle with an initial $250 million, aimed at multifamily / rental residential credit (preferred equity, mezzanine, stretch senior, B-notes). The article does not mention for-sale homebuilding or land.
facts.source_title: Bisnow: GTIS Partners rebrands as Brightshore Capital, launches $250M debt platform

facts.fact: Kiavi: HousingWire reported on 2026-09-01 that Figure had completed the $717 million Kiavi acquisition; Kiavi continues as a Figure subsidiary and CEO Arvind Mohan joined Figure as chief business officer.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Figure completes Kiavi deal, adds investor loans to blockchain platform

facts.fact: Kiavi: Figure Technology Solutions agreed on 2026-06-10 to buy Kiavi's technology and operating platform in a $717 million transaction ($538 million from Figure, funded by a $600 million senior unsecured notes issue; $179 million from Sixth Street, whose joint venture with Figure buys Kiavi's balance-sheet loans). Kiavi had more than $250 million of revenue and more than $100 million of EBITDA in the prior year and has funded more than $30 billion of loans. Its products are investor fix-and-flip (RTL) and DSCR rental loans, so it is not a competitor for builder land.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Figure bolsters first-lien strategy with $717M deal for Kiavi

facts.fact: Blackstone: Commercial Observer (2026-06-01) reports Blackstone told it BREDS, which it describes as a $78 billion real estate debt platform, had already been lending on for-sale home construction for nearly a year before the May 2026 announcement, that the total financing amount is still to be determined, and that this is a first-of-its-kind initiative for the firm. The article does not mention land banking or lot options.
facts.source_title: Commercial Observer: Behind Blackstone's Newfound Commitment to Finance Home Construction (2026-06-01)

facts.fact: Guggenheim (name surfaced by search): IREI (2026-05-21) reports Bedrock Land Finance, a land banking and A&D lender to homebuilders whose parent is TWG Global, was named exclusive land banking partner for the Guggenheim Investments Land Banking Strategy; it describes Guggenheim as having more than $362 billion of total assets. Only the opening of the article is free.
facts.source_title: IREI: Bedrock named exclusive land banking partner for Guggenheim Investments (2026-05-21)

facts.fact: Guggenheim (name surfaced by search): Guggenheim Investments' own news page announces a land banking finance platform that provides land banking financing to homebuilders in high-growth markets through a relationship with Bedrock Land Finance, a residential land development originator and servicer. The page says Bedrock has active projects covering more than 7,500 single-family lots nationally and works with many of the leading public homebuilders; it names no builders, dollar target or capital source. The page itself is undated; trade coverage dates the announcement to 2026-05-19/21.
facts.source_title: Guggenheim Investments: Expands Real Estate Capabilities with Land Banking Finance Platform (2026-05-19)

facts.fact: Blackstone: on 2026-05-11 Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies (BREDS) announced a homebuilder lending platform expected to support construction of more than 50,000 for-sale homes a year, run through BREDS portfolio company Brio Homebuilder Solutions plus unnamed third-party partners. Coverage describes multi-year programmatic builder relationships but does not say whether the product is land banking, land/lot loans or construction loans; no dollar size or builder names were given.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Blackstone homebuilder lending platform (2026-05-11)

facts.fact: Hearthstone: FivePoint Holdings bought 75% of Hearthstone Residential Holdings in mid-2025 (founder Mark Porath kept 25%); at that point Hearthstone managed over $2.6 billion and had funded more than 173,000 homes and lots. On 2026-03-02 the Orange County Business Journal reported that FivePoint and Blue Owl Capital plan to buy up to $1.7 billion of US residential land through Hearthstone: Blue Owl funds provide the capital and earn warrants on FivePoint shares at $7, vesting as contribution milestones from $500 million up to $1.7 billion are met. Hearthstone's AUM was then about $3.4 billion.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: FivePoint and Blue Owl Launch $1.7B Deal

facts.fact: Hearthstone: Orange County Business Journal (2026-03-02) reported that in the first five months under FivePoint, Hearthstone earned $11.8 million of management fees and contributed $3.5 million of net income, and that FivePoint expected $300 million to $500 million of new capital commitments in Q1 2026.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: FivePoint and Blue Owl Launch $1.7B Deal

facts.fact: Blue Owl (name surfaced by search): on 2026-02-10 Five Point Holdings announced that its Hearthstone land-banking platform had formed a residential land banking investment partnership with funds managed by Blue Owl Capital to buy residential homesites and land for national homebuilders. Five Point issued Blue Owl funds warrants at $7.00 per share that vest as cumulative capital contributions hit set thresholds (about 1% dilution if fully exercised). The release gives no dollar size.
facts.source_title: Five Point Holdings press release: new Hearthstone residential land banking investment partnership with Blue Owl managed funds (2026-02-10)

facts.fact: Apollo: on 2025-06-30 Apollo announced Olympus Housing Capital, an Apollo affiliate and new homebuilder finance strategy that funds land acquisition and the development work that turns entitled residential land into finished lots, for both public and private builders. The release names no fund size, product names or builder customers.
facts.source_title: Apollo press release: Apollo Announces Olympus Housing Capital (2025-06-30)

facts.fact: Apollo: Apollo is also a land-bank customer through its builder. Apollo funds have been majority shareholder of The New Home Company (carried as Risewell Homes in the Builder 100 list, the name Commercial Observer also uses for Apollo's builder) since 2021 and committed $650 million of new equity to its all-cash acquisition of Landsea Homes ($11.30 a share, about $1.2 billion, announced May 2025), with Millrose Properties buying select Landsea land and optioning it back to the combined builder. The article calls Millrose a land banking affiliate of Apollo; that wording conflicts with Millrose's public status as a Lennar spin-off externally managed by Kennedy Lewis, so read it as loose trade-press phrasing rather than an ownership fact.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: New Home-Landsea Deal Redraws Builder Power Map (2025-05-13)

facts.fact: Hearthstone: reported assets under management were about $3.4 billion in March 2026 (OCBJ) and still about $3.4 billion in FivePoint's Q3 2026 release of 2026-10-22, up from over $2.6 billion at the mid-2025 acquisition. Inference from those two sources: AUM grew about 30% in the first months under FivePoint and has been flat through the first nine months of 2026 despite the $1.7 billion Blue Owl programme.
facts.source_title: Five Point Holdings 8-K Ex. 99.1, Q3 2026 results (compared with OCBJ 2026-03-02)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: at 2026-09-30 liquidity was about $1.3 billion ($657.0 million unrestricted cash plus $657.8 million available on its senior unsecured revolver); debt was $794.2 million with no senior note maturity until fiscal 2028; net debt to total capital 6.7%; stockholders' equity $1,916.2 million (book value $37.56 per share, up 8% year on year).
facts.source_title: Forestar 8-K Ex. 99.1, fiscal 2026 Q4 and full-year results (2026-10-29)

facts.fact: Forestar Group: capital structure at 2026-09-30 was a $715 million senior unsecured revolver (undrawn; $57.2 million of letters of credit; uncommitted accordion to $1 billion; $650 million matures 2029-12-18, $65 million matured 2026-10-28; commitments raised $25 million in October 2025 and $50 million in March 2026), $300 million of 5.0% senior notes due 2028-03-01 and $500 million of 6.5% senior notes due 2033-03-15. A $750 million equity shelf (including a $300 million at-the-market program) was untouched in fiscal 2026.
facts.source_title: Forestar 10-K for fiscal year ended 2026-09-30, debt and equity notes

facts.fact: Hearthstone: FivePoint's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-22) still shows about $3.4 billion of Hearthstone assets under management. Hearthstone segment management-fee revenue was $6.5 million in Q3 2026 and $18.2 million for the nine months; segment pre-tax profit was $3.0 million and $7.8 million. The release gives no figure for capital funded under the Blue Owl programme.
facts.source_title: Five Point Holdings 8-K Ex. 99.1, Q3 2026 results (2026-10-22)

facts.fact: Avila Real Estate Capital (AREC): by 2026-09-01 it had provided a $305 million facility to an unnamed California master-plan developer (more than 3,000 lots; horizontal and vertical funding; about $700 million across two AREC financings to that borrower), syndicated to banks and family offices in Israel, Brazil, Kuwait and Japan. Tony Avila said Fund Two had reached its $1 billion target; named investors in it include D.R. Horton, Toll Brothers, Century Communities, LGI Homes, Dream Finders Homes and DRB Group. AREC says it has financed more than 18,000 lots against a goal of 100,000 in five years.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: AREC $305M California land facility

facts.fact: Walton Global: AltsWire (2026-06-11) puts Walton at $4.54 billion of total assets and more than 85,000 acres under ownership, management and administration in the US and Canada, and says its Builder Land Finance Fund III (launched July 2025) is a private credit offering targeting $250 million with projected returns of 9% to 11.5%; a Shariah-compliant U.S. Land Income & Growth Fund for offshore investors followed in March 2026. Walton funds its builder programme from retail / private-wealth channels rather than institutional mandates.
facts.source_title: AltsWire: Walton Global adds 525 builder-direct lots in three states

facts.fact: Guggenheim (name surfaced by search): CRE Daily (2026-05-28) reports that Bedrock Land Finance, Guggenheim Investments' land-banking partner, plans to fund up to $5 billion of residential development projects over the coming years; treat that as a target, not committed capital. A search snippet of the press release (not opened, so unconfirmed) adds that Bedrock had already committed over $1 billion to 16 builders and developers.
facts.source_title: CRE Daily: PGIM Bets Big on Land Banking as Homebuilders Seek Flexibility (2026-05-28)

facts.fact: PGIM / insurance capital (reader's own partner, included because insurance capital was on the checklist): CRE Daily (2026-05-28) reports Prudential Financial's asset-management arm has backed roughly $4 billion of residential land-bank deals and completed seven transactions through a partnership with Domain Real Estate Partners begun in 2025. No Pacific Life land-banking activity surfaced in any search.
facts.source_title: CRE Daily: PGIM Bets Big on Land Banking as Homebuilders Seek Flexibility (2026-05-28)

facts.fact: GTIS Partners: on 2026-04-08 GTIS and Hovnanian Enterprises announced a $200 million homebuilding joint venture: GTIS vehicles put in $150 million and Hovnanian $50 million (25%). It covers seven for-sale communities in five states with about 907 homes left to deliver, about $545 million of projected build-out cost and about $617 million of home value; 125 homes (about $82 million) were sold but not closed at closing. This is an equity JV on communities already under construction, not a lot-option land bank. The announcement says it takes the GTIS-Hovnanian portfolio to $1.5 billion and the JV platform to about $8 billion of total home value.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: GTIS-Hovnanian JV announcement

facts.fact: Avila Real Estate Capital (name surfaced by search; builder-backed lender rather than a large alternative manager): AREC's second debt fund reached about $200 million of commitments toward a $1 billion target at its second close (reported 2026-03-09), anchored by Hillwood Communities, with D.R. Horton, Toll Brothers and Century Communities investing as limited partners. It lends land development and AD&C capital to developers and private builders and aims to originate about $1 billion a year.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Horton, Toll, Century back AREC Fund as AD&C credit tightens (2026-03-09)

facts.fact: Blue Owl (name surfaced by search): the Orange County Business Journal (2026-03-02) reports the Hearthstone-Blue Owl partnership could buy up to $1.7 billion of US residential land, with Blue Owl's warrants vesting from $500 million of contributed capital up to $1.7 billion. It reports Hearthstone's assets under management at about $3.4 billion (up from about $2.6 billion when FivePoint bought 75% of it in 2025) and that FivePoint expected $300-500 million of new capital commitments in Q1 2026. The $1.7 billion is a ceiling, not committed capital.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: FivePoint and Blue Owl launch $1.7B deal (2026-03-02)

facts.fact: Kiavi: closed a $350 million rated securitization of residential transition loans on 2026-02-19 (its sixth rated deal and 24th on the LHOME shelf; two-year revolving period; rated by Morningstar DBRS; more than 5x oversubscribed), projected to add about $1.2 billion of funding capacity. Kiavi reports record 2025 originations of $7.8 billion (up 20%) and more than $30 billion funded to date. Its business is fix-and-flip / bridge loans to investors plus a ground-up construction product; nothing found on land banking or lot financing for homebuilders.
facts.source_title: Kiavi press release: closes $350M rated RTL securitization

facts.fact: Walton Global: on 2026-02-12 it launched The American Builder Growth and Income Fund, seeking up to $500 million through independent broker-dealers, family offices and RIAs. The fund mixes secured land loans to homebuilders (made through Walton's Builder Land Financing platform) with land acquisition for appreciation.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: launches The American Builder Growth and Income Fund

facts.fact: Avila Real Estate Capital (AREC): held a $100 million first close on its second builder debt fund in November 2025, anchored by Hillwood Communities, with a $1 billion target by mid-2026. It makes first-lien land development loans and homebuilder revolvers for for-sale housing only. Its first debt fund closed July 2025 with over $700 million of commitments and co-investments.
facts.source_title: HousingWire / The Builder's Daily: Hillwood backs new homebuilding fund as AD&C credit tightens

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital originations are funded by Apollo-managed funds and affiliated balance sheets, per the launch release. The release does not name Athene as the funding source (Athene appears only in Apollo's standard company description), so an Athene link is not publicly stated.
facts.source_title: Apollo press release: Apollo Announces Olympus Housing Capital (2025-06-30)

facts.fact: Pretium: Pretium closed its first homebuilder finance fund with $550 million of equity commitments in January 2025, aiming to originate up to $5 billion of loans to US homebuilders by recycling capital over the fund's life.
facts.source_title: Alternatives Watch: Pretium launches $550 million homebuilder finance fund (2025-01-16)

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital's website lists an 11-person leadership roster under CEO Andrew Brausa, including Senior Vice Presidents Aimee Martin and Troy Wahlberg, Controller Alexa Brennan, Associate Vice Presidents Matt Caldwell and Donna Ransom (Closings), four senior associates and one associate. Headcount is a count of the names shown on the page on 2026-11-19 (the page was truncated, so the list may be incomplete).
facts.source_title: Olympus Housing Capital website (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Starwood: the Starwood-Trez land lending partnership was announced by Anthony Murphy, managing director at Starwood Capital, with Trez Capital co-CEOs John D. Hutchinson (global head of origination) and John Maragliano (CFO). Bisnow notes Starwood had earlier bought several Texas master-planned communities from Hines (an $800 million deal) in which Trez had been Hines's partner.

Horton EVP and Treasurer (1991-2014), joined the board on 2026-11-01 as a Horton designee.

facts.fact: Brookfield: Warren Krug is chief investment officer of Brookfield Residential and was quoted on 2026-10-16 saying large 2026 housing deals are replacing shorter-term private-equity capital with longer-dated owners; the same article cites Brookfield's Newland and Kolter transactions as examples of investing in land operators before buying them. gaps: Apollo / Olympus Housing Capital: fund size, named builder customers, lot counts, option-fee yields and whether Athene is the balance sheet are not publicly disclosed (Apollo release, IPE, Commercial Observer checked). olympushc.com could not be opened (WebFetch domain check rate-limited).

Blackstone: the primary press release on blackstone.com returned a bot-check page and the BusinessWire and The Real Deal copies returned HTTP 403, so Blackstone rows rest on trade-press copies (IREI, HousingWire, Commercial Observer). Product mix (land banking vs land loans vs construction loans), dollar size, Brio Homebuilder Solutions leadership and builder names are not public in what could be opened.

Värde Partners: current platform name, size, lot count and builder list for its land-banking business are not publicly disclosed. Värde's site names no branded homebuilder-finance platform; the last announced deals are David Weekley (2024-04), American Homes 4 Rent ($500 million, 2022), Taylor Morrison (over $1 billion, 2021) and Dream Finders ($100 million, seen in search results only). Whether those facilities are still drawing in 2026 could not be confirmed from free sources.

Brookfield: no 2025-2026 press release, fund name, size or builder list for Brookfield's land financing / lot banking was found, and no successor to Andrew Brausa was identified. brookfield.com would not load (domain check rate-limited, then 404 on the one URL tried); the PERE 2021 article is paywalled.

KKR: no public evidence of US homebuilder land banking or land finance in 2025-2026 (searches: 'KKR OR Ares OR Oaktree land banking homebuilder facility 2025 2026'; 'KKR homebuilder land financing lots land bank builder 2026'). Only a UK living-sector lending JV with Puma (GBP 500 million, March 2026) appeared in a search snippet; nothing citable was opened.

Ares: no public evidence of homebuilder land banking or land finance in 2025-2026 (searches: 'Ares Management residential land lot banking homebuilder land banking'; the combined KKR/Ares/Oaktree queries). Only a 2010 equity investment in builder City Ventures surfaced; nothing citable was opened.

Carlyle, Sixth Street, Cerberus, Centerbridge: no public evidence of homebuilder land banking or land finance in 2025-2026 (searches: 'Carlyle OR Sixth Street OR Cerberus OR Centerbridge homebuilder land banking OR lot option OR land finance 2025 2026'; 'Sixth Street OR Cerberus OR Fortress OR Carlyle homebuilder land financing lots builder facility announced 2026'). Results were unrelated (a Carlyle/Sixth Street BDC CLO venture, a Centerbridge commercial property stake). No firm-specific page was opened, and planned one-firm follow-up searches could not be run because the shared web-search budget ran out.

Bain Capital: no public evidence found (search: 'Pretium OR Bain Capital OR Fortress homebuilder land banking OR finished lots OR builder finance facility 2025 2026'); the single-firm follow-up search was blocked by the search budget, so this is a light check.

PIMCO, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Invesco, Rockpoint: no public evidence found (search: 'Goldman Sachs OR Invesco OR Rockpoint OR PIMCO land banking homebuilder 2025 2026'); results returned only PGIM, Guggenheim and general market pieces. Light check: one combined query, no firm-specific page opened.

Pacific Life: no public evidence of land-bank financing found (search: 'Pacific Life OR insurance company land banking homebuilder lots financing 2026'). Insurance capital that did surface: PGIM (via Domain) and Guggenheim (via Bedrock).

Blue Owl / Hearthstone: capital actually contributed to date, yields and builder names are not disclosed; the $1.7 billion figure is the top warrant-vesting threshold reported by OCBJ, and the Five Point release gives no dollar size.

Starwood / Trez: loan sizes, pricing, borrower names and which Starwood vehicle funds the partnership are not disclosed. No 2026 Starwood Land lot-option (land banking) program was found; its 2025 Texas master-planned community purchases (Hines portfolio, Land Tejas) are land-developer positions rather than builder financing, and were seen mainly in search results.

Pretium: fund names beyond the first $550 million fund, loan counts, pricing and borrower names are not public in the free text opened; the Alternatives Watch article is paywalled after the first lines. No evidence Pretium does lot-option land banking.

Method limits: the shared web-search budget was exhausted about two-thirds of the way through, so several firms got one combined query only; blackstone.com, businesswire.com, therealdeal.com, nationalmortgageprofessional.com, builderonline.com and advisorperspectives.com returned 403 or bot checks and were not worked around.

Web search budget for this run (shared across agents) was exhausted after about 15 searches, so the wider candidate list could not be checked. NOT researched at all (no finding either way): Landsea / Lot Bank-type vehicles, Raven / Rockpoint, Sumitomo Forestry / Crescent, Columnar Investments, Lotus Capital Partners, Tricon, BTI Partners, Toll Brothers' and Taylor Morrison's named land-bank partners, ResiBuilt / Pretium, Bain / Arch-type JVs, AmeriFirst, Trez Capital (trezcapital.com/news returned 404), Texas Capital / Western Alliance / Flagstar builder finance, Anchor Loans, CoreVest, Roc360, Toorak, Rialto, Emerald, JEN Partners, McCourt, Resmark, Presidio Residential Capital, Tavistock, Castle Rock, MSD / BDT, Sagebrook. These need a follow-up pass.

Walton Global: no builder is named in any 2026 Finished Lot Program / Builder Land Finance release; option premium, deposit and takedown terms are not published. The phrase 'exit-focused' was not found on the pages opened. Builder Land Finance Fund III ($250 million target, 9% to 11.5% projected return, launched July 2025) is cited only via AltsWire; the BusinessWire original (businesswire.com/news/home/20250717509861) returned 403, as did GlobeSt's piece on the $500 million fund.

Walton Global: total builder-land-finance volume to date (lots, dollars, number of builders) not publicly disclosed on its site; the $4.54 billion total assets / 85,000 acres figures come from AltsWire, not a Walton page opened in this run.

Hearthstone: capital actually funded under the Blue Owl programme, number of builders and projects, option-fee rates and named builder counterparties for 2025-2026 are not disclosed in FivePoint's Q3 2026 release or the OCBJ article.
